Gifted Manipuri musician beaten to death for objecting to noise outside Delhi home
articles.description: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a gifted guitarist, died after being beaten outside his home.  He had gone to stop intoxicated men creating a disturbance near his residence.  Singh was found in a critical state and rushed to the hospital.  Doctors found his blood pressure had fallen critically low.  He succumbed to his injuries Monday morning during treatment.

For two hours, flames leaped 150 to 200 feet into the sky until the force of the escaping gas extinguished itself.

articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex tanks over 330 points, NSE Nifty50 opens below 23,700
articles.full_text: Stock market today: Rupee falls 10 paise against US dollar Stock market today: Stock recommendations for September 8 - check list Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty might open on a muted note on Tuesday, with GIFT Nifty pointing to a flat-to-negative start. GIFT Nifty was trading at 23,783, down 43.5 points, or 0.18%, from the previous close. Crude oil prices rising above $97 a barrel and continued tensions between the US and Iran are likely to remain key factors for the market. Investors are also watching the impact of higher oil prices on sentiment. The cautious start comes after equities failed to hold on to the gains from the previous session. The Sensex fell 382.62 points, or 0.50%, to close at 76,132.81, while the Nifty dropped 118.55 points, or 0.50%, to end at 23,779.15. Selling was seen across most sectors, pulling both benchmarks lower. Asian markets were mixed, with South Korea and Taiwan among the markets showing gains, while Hong Kong and Australia traded lower. The Hang Seng Index fell 141.87 points, or 0.56%, to 25,271.25. South Korea’s Kospi gained 133.69 points, or 1.91%, to 7,129.08, while Taiwan’s index rose 184.81 points, or 0.39%, to 47,511.08. Japan’s Nikkei was up 120.73 points, or 0.18%, at 66,520.57, while Shanghai gained 9.773 points, or 0.25%, to 3,942.473. Shenzhen was almost flat, down 0.02%. Australia’s ASX 200 fell 0.43%, while New Zealand’s NZX 50 declined 0.63%. Malaysia and Singapore also traded lower, while Thailand’s SETI was unchanged. India’s Nifty 50 was unchanged at 23,779.15. Oil prices edged higher as the conflict in the Middle East continued to intensify, raising concerns over global supplies. Brent crude rose 0.05%, or $0.05, to $97.05 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 1.03%, or $0.94, to $92.42 a barrel. The latest gains came after Iran warned that it would retaliate against any further US attacks on its assets. The warning added to concerns that the conflict could continue and put energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the Gulf at risk. The Strait of Hormuz remains a key focus for oil traders as tensions around the major route for global crude shipments remain high. Traders have been building a risk premium into oil prices because of the uncertainty around supplies. Brent had already climbed to its highest level since July 24 in the previous session. Indian equities ended the previous session in red, with the benchmark Sensex declining 382.62 points, or 0.50%, to settle at 76,132.81. The index had fallen as much as 544.91 points, or 0.71%, touching a low of 75,970.52. NSE Nifty also closed 118.55 points, or 0.50%, lower at 23,779.15. Of the 30 Sensex constituents, 23 ended in the red while seven advanced. Infosys was the biggest laggard among the Sensex stocks, falling 3.81%, while Tech Mahindra, Tata Steel, Bajaj Finserv, UltraTech Cement and Tata Consultancy Services also declined. Larsen & Toubro, Bharti Airtel, Maruti and Power Grid were among the gainers.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

articles.title: Parvathy Thiruvothu blames celebrity silence during student protests
articles.description: Parvathy Thiruvothu emphasizes the importance of film celebrities standing by the youth during tough times. She argues that artists should not be passive while facing serious challenges. The actor perceives it as unjust for celebrities to overlook the struggles of their supporters, highlighting that youthful energy is what elevates stars. Thiruvothu believes artists have a crucial responsibility to raise awareness about significant issues affecting people.
